Green: **625 total, 625 passing, 0 failing** (exit 0).

## What was actually broken

Out of the ~700 lines of output, there were only **3 real failures**, all in the `order totals` suite and all the same root cause:

| case | expected | actual |
|---|---|---|
| `orderTotal(12000, 15, 0.0825)` | 11042 | 11190 |
| `orderTotal(8650, 20, 0.05)` | 7266 | 7353 |
| `orderTotal(33400, 10, 0.2)` | 36072 | 36740 |

`orderTotal` in `src/pricing.js:39` computed the tax off the **pre-discount** base:

```js
const discounted = applyDiscount(cents, discountPct);
const tax = roundCents(cents * taxRate);   // <- cents, not discounted
return discounted + tax;
```

That contradicts the function's own doc comment ("Tax is charged on the amount the customer pays"), and it overcharges tax on the discounted portion — the delta is exactly `discount × taxRate`.

The fix routes the discounted subtotal through the existing `applyTax`:

```js
const discounted = applyDiscount(cents, discountPct);
return applyTax(discounted, taxRate);
```

Worth noting why this hid for so long: of the 69 rows in that suite, 66 have either a zero discount or a zero tax, and the bug is invisible unless **both** are non-zero. Only the three hand-written rows at `cases.js:80-82` have that combination. If you add more order-total coverage, make sure it's in that both-non-zero region — the generated rows can't catch ordering mistakes.

The other eight suites (line totals, discounts, taxes, volume tiers, refunds, shipping, loyalty, rounding) were passing the whole time; the wall of text was just the verbose reporter printing an `ok` line per case.
